feedback: 1) Semantic fidelity / reachability: silencing is driven by siren_ringing, but the RM checks (switch_toggled & !siren_ringing) on the transition out of u1. In u1, switch_toggled always coincides with !siren_ringing (a toggle when ringing silences it, so siren_ringing is false that step; a toggle when silent is impossible to reach u1... wait, actually u1 is entered only via siren_ringing). However, a step could show switch_toggled=true with siren_ringing=false but the toggle occurred while the siren was silent—this cannot happen in u1 since u1 is only entered when the siren is ringing and the siren stays ringing until toggled. So the silencing transition is reachable and correct. The real defect is reward design and event coverage. 2) Silencing has NO reward: R(u1, switch_toggled&!siren_ringing, u0) is missing—only the entry reward 0.1 on ring and exit 1.0 exist. The task 'silence the siren every time it rings' should reward the silencing transition; as written the agent is rewarded 0.1 merely for letting the siren ring, with no incentive to toggle. 3) Reward safety: R(u0, siren_ringing, u1)=0.1 is unsafe — it rewards the siren STARTING (an uncontrollable, scheduled event), potentially encouraging policies to dither/avoid finishing so the siren rings more often for repeated 0.1 without ever silencing; net-sum reward hacking. Also, exit reward 1.0 ignores whether the siren is silent: since u2 is only entered from u0 (siren silenced or never rang), actually if the agent exits while the siren rings it sits in u1, and (u1, at_exit) is not defined — the else loop keeps it in u1 forever with no terminal reward, so RM reward 0 at the actual final step. That is arguably intended (exit with ringing siren = failure of silencing condition), but the environment pays 1-0.9*fraction only if the siren is silent at exit; aligning RM with that requires checking siren_ringing is false at exit, which u0-entry does enforce. Acceptable. 4) Reachability of u2: u2 reachable from u0 via at_exit; fine. FINAL_STATES nonempty and u2 declared; accepted structurally. 5) Irrelevant events: box events (holding_box, box_fell) are irrelevant to this task — handled by the per-state else self-loops: yes, (u0,else)->u0, (u1,else)->u1, (u2,else)->u2 cover holding_box, box_fell, and switch_toggled-while-silent (in u0 toggle&!ringing is folded into else->u0, fine). 6) Ordered transition coverage: 'else' semantics must mean 'any event not matching a listed transition'; in u0, if switch_toggled&!siren_ringing occurs it falls to else->u0 — correct since toggle of a silent siren is a no-op. In u1, a toggle while STILL ringing? Impossible in one step (toggle silences immediately). OK. 7) Missing silencing reward is the main fixable flaw; if silencing is meant to be purely enforced by gating the exit reward, that is defensible, but then the entry reward 0.1 on ring remains unsafe reward shaping for an uncontrollable event. Minimum required changes: either remove R(u0,siren_ringing,u1) or add a reward on the silencing transition (e.g., R(u1,switch_toggled&!siren_ringing,u0) = +0.1) and keep progress bounded/dense; as-is, the machine rewards an uncontrollable event and gives zero incentive for the actual silencing action.
